To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dispersal of gypsy moth eggs and larvae is influenced by the quality of the environment in which the eggs are laid.

(1) the majority of first-instar larvae disperse; (2) large larvae are more likely than small larvae to disperse in the presence of preferred food; (3) small larvae disperse more than large larvae when food is scarce or absent; and (4) the size of first-instar eggs may affect the dispersal patterns of first-instar and subsequent generations of larvae.
